Solid port of the legacy Kea/dhcpd inputs from src/maasserver/dhcp.py into the service layer: vlan/relay discovery, managed-subnet grouping, family filtering, HA roles, host reservations and per-subnet DNS/NTP selection all match the legacy semantics closely, and the new tests exercise the important branches (relay vs serving vlan, HA role independence, tie-breaks, dedup). Clause-factory additions are consistent with existing patterns, InterfaceRelationshipTable mirrors the Django model (columns, deferrable FKs, index names), and `use_rack_proxy`/`ntp_*` config keys all exist in ConfigurationsService. Main concerns: (1) `_get_best_interface_with_ip_on_vlan` is a query hot spot — it runs one `get_for_interfaces` per interface plus `subnets.get_by_id` and `ipranges.get_many` per IP, and it is re-executed for every subnet and again per HA rack per subnet; the legacy code avoided exactly this with prefetch_related, so consider batching/prefetching once per request. (2) `_get_ip_address_for_rack_controller` diverges from legacy `get_ip_address_for_rack_controller`: legacy only considered interfaces that already have a STICKY/AUTO IP strictly on the VLAN, whereas the port picks the best interface from a wider pool (relay-vlan or DISCOVERED matches) and only then applies the strict `subnet.vlan_id == vlan.id` filter — so it can select a preferred interface that has no qualifying address and make `_get_ha_config` raise where legacy would have returned the address from a different interface. (3) `_make_interface_hostname` resolves the node via `current_config_id == interface.node_config_id` and then asserts; host reservations iterate interfaces from `get_for_ip` across the whole DB, so a stale node_config (interfaces keep their original config while the node's current config moves on) turns into an AssertionError/500 — legacy used `interface.node_config.node` which cannot miss. Minor: the `ntp_servers` expression in the return duplicates `default_dns_servers` verbatim, and `services/interfaces.py:get_parents` uses `self.repository` where the rest of the class uses `self.interface_repository`. No security issues found: parameterized queries throughout, no secret handling, and the OSError path around hostname resolution is handled.

src/maasservicelayer/services/dhcp.py.422: Performance: this runs `get_for_interfaces` once per interface, plus `subnets_service.get_by_id` and `ipranges_service.get_many` per IP (line 433), and `_get_best_interface_with_ip_on_vlan` is invoked for every subnet in `get_kea_dhcp_data_for_agent` and again per HA rack inside `_get_ip_address_for_rack_controller`. On a rack with many interfaces/subnets this becomes O(subnets × interfaces × ips) queries per request. The legacy implementation this replaces (maasserver/dhcp.py `get_interfaces_with_ip_on_vlan`) used prefetch_related to keep this at a constant query count; consider fetching all interfaces' IPs in one query and caching subnet→dynamic-range counts for the duration of the call.
src/maasservicelayer/services/dhcp.py.542: Divergence from legacy `get_ip_address_for_rack_controller` (maasserver/dhcp.py): legacy built the candidate pool with `ip_is_on_vlan`, i.e. only interfaces that already have a STICKY/AUTO IP strictly on `vlan`, then applied `get_best_interface`. Here the pool comes from `_get_best_interface_with_ip_on_vlan`, which also accepts relay-vlan matches and the DISCOVERED fallback, and the strict `STICKY/AUTO + ip_subnet.vlan_id == vlan.id` check (lines 550-556) only inspects the one selected interface. When the type preference picks a bond that only qualifies via the relay VLAN, `_get_ha_config` raises `ValidationException` even though another interface on the VLAN has a usable address — legacy would have returned it. Consider filtering candidates to interfaces with a STICKY/AUTO address on the exact VLAN before the preference loop.
src/maasservicelayer/services/dhcp.py.370: This re-derives exactly the same value as `default_dns_servers` (line 232-238: `dict.fromkeys(str(ip.ip) for ip in rack_ips if ip.ip is not None and ip.subnet_id in subnet_ids)`). Reuse the variable instead of duplicating the expression; otherwise the two can silently drift if one filter changes.
src/maasservicelayer/services/dhcp.py.666: This assert can fail: host reservations iterate every interface returned by `get_for_ip`, i.e. across all nodes and config generations. `NodeClauseFactory.with_node_config_id` matches `Node.current_config_id`, so an interface still attached to a historical NodeConfig (its node has since moved to a newer current config) yields `node is None` and turns the whole DHCP payload request into an AssertionError/500. Legacy `make_interface_hostname` used `interface.node_config.node` (direct FK) and handled the missing-config case. Prefer resolving the node through the NodeConfig→node relation, or degrade gracefully (skip the reservation / fall back to `unknown-`) as services/interfaces.py does with `if not node: return`.
src/maasservicelayer/services/dhcp.py.797: Minor: the `(region.id, server.version) in seen_regions` check runs after `get_for_nodes` has already executed, so every additional server in `dns_servers` re-queries the same region's IPs. Hoist the check above the query to avoid the redundant round trips (legacy `get_maas_facing_server_addresses` marks the region only after querying, but it also had no cheap pre-check).

src/maasservicelayer/services/interfaces.83: Use `self.interface_repository` for consistency with the rest of this class (`list_for_node`, `get_interfaces_for_mac`, `get_interfaces_in_fabric`); `self.repository` works because the base class stores the same instance, but the mixed accessor is easy to misread.
